169	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
170	        super().__init__(context)
171	        # Guards `_finalize_unreproducible` to run at most once per run. `after_review()`
172	        # calls it (so the pushed registry includes on-the-fly snippets), then the base
173	        # `apply()` calls it again; the second call is a no-op so a snippet's `authored_at`
174	        # is stamped exactly once and the source and pushed target registries stay identical.
175	        self._unreproducible_finalized = False
176	
177	    # -- after-review snippet push (D-23) -----------------------------------------------
178	
179	    @override
180	    async def after_review(self) -> None:
181	        """Push the install-snippet registry to the target after this job's review and
182	        before `apply()` replays any snippet (D-23), then promote each on-the-fly-authored
183	        item so it is APPLIED — not merely transported — the same run.
184	
185	        Finalize-then-push-then-promote: `_finalize_unreproducible` persists this run's
186	        authored snippets into the SOURCE registry first (idempotent — `apply()` calls it
187	        again as a no-op), then `_push_snippet_registry` copies that file to the target,
188	        and finally `_promote_authored_snippets_to_install` reclassifies each authored
189	        item's diff `REPORT_ONLY -> INSTALL` decided `APPLY` so the unchanged base
190	        `apply()` converges it this run rather than the next one. Promotion runs AFTER the
191	        push so the target already holds the snippet the replay reads. The push depends on
192	        no other job: it moves the file itself and reads neither `config_sync` nor
193	        `folder_sync` state, so disabling either cannot break snippet delivery.
194	        """
195	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
196	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
197	        await self._finalize_unreproducible(self._accepted_plan, self._accepted_outcome)
198	        await self._push_snippet_registry()
199	        self._promote_authored_snippets_to_install()
200	
201	    def _promote_authored_snippets_to_install(self) -> None:
202	        """Reclassify every on-the-fly-authored item's diff `REPORT_ONLY -> INSTALL` and
203	        force its decision to `APPLY`, so the unchanged base `apply()` — which converges
204	        only APPLY-decided, non-`REPORT_ONLY` diffs (`sync_core.py` apply_diffs filter) —
205	        replays the freshly authored snippet THIS run, closing the one-run-too-late gap.
206	
207	        Called from `after_review()` only after the authored snippets are persisted to the
208	        source registry and pushed to the target, so the target holds the snippet by the
209	        time the promoted diff converges. The add-snippet review path records no decision
210	        for the item (`packages.review._review_unreproducible_group`), so the decision must
211	        be forced here in addition to reclassifying the action.
212	
213	        Mutates only in-memory accepted state (a `dataclasses.replace` of the frozen plan
214	        and outcome), so it is safe under dry-run: `apply()`'s dry-run branch previews a
215	        would-install line and issues no converge, preserving ADR-014.
216	        """
217	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
218	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
219	        outcome = self._accepted_outcome
220	        if not outcome.snippets:
221	            return
222	
223	        plan = self._accepted_plan
224	        authored = frozenset(outcome.snippets)
225	        new_diffs = tuple(
226	            replace(diff, action=DiffAction.INSTALL)
227	            if diff.item_id in authored and diff.action is DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY
228	            else diff
229	            for diff in plan.diffs
230	        )
231	        new_decisions = dict(outcome.decisions)
232	        for item_id in authored:
233	            new_decisions[item_id] = Decision.APPLY
234	
235	        self._accepted_plan = replace(plan, diffs=new_diffs)
236	        self._accepted_outcome = replace(outcome, decisions=new_decisions)

238	    async def _push_snippet_registry(self) -> None:
239	        """Copy the source's `~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml` to the target's
240	        own copy under the SSH user's home, mirroring `config_sync._copy_config_to_target`'s
241	        `mkdir -p` -> `echo $HOME` -> `send_file` shape.
242	
243	        `send_file` writes plain SFTP as the SSH user, always under that user's home
244	        (`~/.config/pc-switcher`) — never `/etc` — which is exactly where the registry
245	        belongs, so no `sudo install` staging is needed. A no-op if the source has no
246	        registry file yet (a user who has never authored a snippet) and under dry-run
247	        (ADR-014: a rehearsal transfers nothing).
248	
249	        The push is a WHOLE-FILE overwrite (no per-entry merge). Before it runs,
250	        `_guard_registry_overwrite` compares the target's current registry against the
251	        source's on-disk file (decision 9): a purely additive push (source superset of
252	        target) proceeds silently, while one that would lose or change a target entry
253	        requires explicit confirmation and otherwise aborts the run.
254	        """
255	        if self.context.dry_run:
256	            return
257	
258	        source_path = Path.home() / SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH
259	        if not source_path.exists():
260	            return
261	
262	        await self._guard_registry_overwrite(source_path)
263	
264	        mkdir = await self.target.run_command(
265	            f"mkdir -p {CONFIG_REMOTE_DIR}", mutates="create the pc-switcher config directory on the target"
266	        )
267	        if not mkdir.success:
268	            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to create config directory on target: {mkdir.stderr}")
269	
270	        # send_file needs an absolute remote path, so expand the target's ~ once.
271	        home = await self.target.run_command("echo $HOME")
272	        if not home.success:
273	            raise RuntimeError("Failed to get home directory on target")
274	        absolute_remote_path = f"{home.stdout.strip()}/{SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH}"
275	        await self.target.send_file(
276	            source_path, absolute_remote_path, mutates="push the install-snippet registry to the target"
277	        )
278	
279	    async def _guard_registry_overwrite(self, source_path: Path) -> None:
280	        """Gate the wholesale `package-snippets.yaml` overwrite on the loss/change of any
281	        target entry (decision 9).
282	
283	        The source's on-disk file (the exact bytes about to be sent) is compared against
284	        the target's current registry per `item_id`. The push is purely additive when the
285	        source is a superset of the target — every target entry is present in the source
286	        with an identical body — in which case it proceeds silently, as before. Otherwise
287	        the target holds an entry that a wholesale overwrite would LOSE (absent from the
288	        source) or CHANGE (a differing body); the user is shown exactly which entries and
289	        must confirm. Declining, or a non-interactive run that cannot confirm, aborts the
290	        whole sync (`SyncAbortedByUser`) so the user can consolidate the two registries by
291	        hand and re-run — the tool never silently discards a snippet only the target has.
292	        """
293	        source_snippets = load_snippets_from_text(source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
294	        target_snippets = await SnippetRegistry(self.target).load()
295	
296	        lost = [snippet for item_id, snippet in target_snippets.items() if item_id not in source_snippets]
297	        changed = [
298	            (snippet, source_snippets[item_id])
299	            for item_id, snippet in target_snippets.items()
300	            if item_id in source_snippets and source_snippets[item_id].body != snippet.body
301	        ]
302	        if not lost and not changed:
303	            return  # purely additive — source is a superset of the target
304	
305	        assert self.context.confirmer is not None, (
306	            "a non-additive snippet registry overwrite needs a confirmer to gate it"
307	        )
308	        approved = await self.context.confirmer.confirm(
309	            title="Snippet registry overwrite is not purely additive",
310	            message=self._render_overwrite_diff(lost, changed),
311	            # No override flag exists: a lossy overwrite is only ever approved by a human
312	            # answering the prompt, so `allow=False` makes any non-interactive run refuse
313	            # (and thus abort) rather than silently overwrite.
314	            allow=False,
315	            allow_flag="manual registry consolidation",
316	            log_extra={"job": self.name, "host": "source"},
317	        )
318	        if not approved:
319	            raise SyncAbortedByUser(
320	                "snippet registry overwrite declined: the target holds snippet entries "
321	                "absent from or differing in the source that a wholesale push would lose "
322	                "or change; consolidate the two registries by hand and re-run"
323	            )
324	
325	    @staticmethod
326	    def _render_overwrite_diff(lost: list[Snippet], changed: list[tuple[Snippet, Snippet]]) -> str:
327	        """Rich-markup body naming every target entry a wholesale push would lose or change.
328	
329	        Every snippet field is untrusted package-manager/user text, so each is
330	        `rich.markup.escape`d before it reaches the confirmer's `Panel` — a body or label
331	        containing `[...]` must not be parsed as console markup (T-02-02).
332	        """
333	
334	        def body_lines(body: str, indent: str) -> list[str]:
335	            return [f"{indent}{escape(line)}" for line in (body.splitlines() or [""])]
336	
337	        lines = ["The target's snippet registry holds entries this overwrite would discard or replace:", ""]
338	        for snippet in lost:
339	            lines.append(f"  LOST     {escape(snippet.label)}  ({escape(snippet.item_id)})")
340	            lines.extend(body_lines(snippet.body, "             "))
341	        for target_snippet, source_snippet in changed:
342	            lines.append(f"  CHANGED  {escape(target_snippet.label)}  ({escape(target_snippet.item_id)})")
343	            lines.append("             target (to be replaced):")
344	            lines.extend(body_lines(target_snippet.body, "               "))
345	            lines.append("             source (incoming):")
346	            lines.extend(body_lines(source_snippet.body, "               "))
347	        lines += [
348	            "",
349	            "Continuing overwrites the target's registry wholesale. Decline to abort and "
350	            "consolidate the two registries by hand.",
351	        ]
352	        return "\n".join(lines)

354	    # -- Detection (D-18/D-19), all on the source ---------------------------------------
355	
356	    async def _scan_no_candidate_apt_packages(self, manual_names: Sequence[str]) -> list[UnreproducibleItem]:
357	        """D-18: manually-installed packages whose SOURCE's own `apt-cache` has no
358	        candidate at all — installed via `dpkg -i` of a bare `.deb`, never registered with
359	        any configured repository. Runs the job's OWN `apt-cache policy` (D-18), never
360	        apt_sync's.
361	        """
362	        if not manual_names:
363	            return []
364	
365	        quoted = " ".join(shlex.quote(name) for name in manual_names)
366	        result = await self.source.run_command(f"apt-cache policy {quoted}")
367	        no_candidate = _packages_with_no_candidate(result.stdout)
368	        return [
369	            UnreproducibleItem(origin="apt-no-candidate", identifier=name, label=f"{name} (no apt candidate)")
370	            for name in sorted(no_candidate)
371	        ]
372	
373	    async def _scan_unowned_installs(self) -> list[UnreproducibleItem]:
374	        """D-18/D-19: paths under `/usr/local` and `/opt` that no dpkg package owns —
375	        software an install script dropped there directly, bypassing apt entirely.
376	
377	        One batched `find` over `_UNOWNED_SCAN_ROOTS` names every candidate path, then one
378	        batched `dpkg -S` over those candidates decides ownership; a path absent from the
379	        `dpkg -S` output is unowned. Both steps run on the SOURCE (D-18) — a fact about
380	        what the source machine has installed, not the target.
381	        """
382	        quoted_roots = " ".join(shlex.quote(root) for root in _UNOWNED_SCAN_ROOTS)
383	        listing = await self.source.run_command(f"find {quoted_roots} -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 2>/dev/null")
384	        candidates = _lines(listing.stdout)
385	        if not candidates:
386	            return []
387	
388	        quoted_paths = " ".join(shlex.quote(path) for path in candidates)
389	        ownership = await self.source.run_command(f"dpkg -S {quoted_paths}")
390	        owned = _owned_paths_from_dpkg_s(ownership.stdout)
391	
392	        return [
393	            UnreproducibleItem(origin="unowned-path", identifier=path, label=path)
394	            for path in sorted(set(candidates) - owned)
395	        ]

397	    # -- plan() / converge() ------------------------------------------------------------
398	
399	    @override
400	    async def capture_source_items(self) -> Sequence[UnreproducibleItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
401	        """The source's unreproducible items: apt-no-candidate packages plus unowned
402	        `/usr/local`/`/opt` installs (D-18). `apt-mark showmanual` runs once here and its
403	        result feeds the no-candidate scan.
404	
405	        This job overrides `plan()` and never routes through `PackageSyncJob.diff_items`'s
406	        apt-package-shaped dispatch, so widening this hook's item type is safe (same
407	        reasoning as `SnapSyncJob.capture_source_items`).
408	        """
409	        manual = await self.source.run_command("apt-mark showmanual")
410	        manual_names = _lines(manual.stdout)
411	        return [
412	            *await self._scan_no_candidate_apt_packages(manual_names),
413	            *await self._scan_unowned_installs(),
414	        ]
415	
416	    @override
417	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[UnreproducibleItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
418	        """No target-side manifest exists for unreproducible items: they are always
419	        source-held (they describe what the SOURCE machine has installed), and convergence
420	        is driven by the shared snippet registry, not by a diff against target state. The
421	        empty result keeps the abstract hook satisfied without a meaningless target query.
422	        """
423	        return []
424	
425	    @override
426	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
427	        """Detect -> filter inert -> diff against the SOURCE's snippet registry. Read-only.
428	
429	        An item already recorded machine-specific on the SOURCE is dropped by

1	"""Per-action confirmation gate behind `--confirm-each-command`.
2	
3	A package sync run converges dozens of small mutating commands — `apt-get install`,
4	`snap remove`, `sudo install` into `/etc/apt`, an SFTP push of the snippet registry — each
5	of which was approved only in aggregate, as a ticked line in a batched review. This gate
6	inserts one prompt before every single one of them, showing the EXACT operation about to
7	happen: the literal shell command as it will be passed to the shell, or the local path and
8	remote destination of a file transfer. Nothing is paraphrased or reconstructed for display,
9	because a display string that differs from what runs is worse than no display at all.
10	
11	Distinct from `pcswitcher.confirmer.Confirmer`, which gates ONE coarse decision per run
12	(first-sync overwrite, out-of-order topology) and falls back to an `--allow-*` flag when
13	nobody is there to answer. This gate has no such fallback and never auto-proceeds: it is
14	opt-in per run and refused outright without a TTY (`cli.sync`), because a gate that
15	auto-proceeds when unanswerable is precisely the failure it exists to prevent.
16	
17	Two outcomes only, with no default (the user must type one): proceed, or abort the whole
18	sync. There is deliberately no "skip this command" — a single reviewed item can span
19	several commands (apt source stage-then-promote, snap install-then-switch-channel), so
20	skipping one of them leaves that item half-applied, which is a worse state than either
21	finishing it or stopping.
22	
23	Generic on purpose, and invoked from exactly one place: `pcswitcher.executor`. Any caller
24	— job, orchestrator, helper — gates a write by passing `mutates="..."` to the executor
25	method it already uses, so there is no second API to remember and no per-job wiring. The
26	executor supplies `job` (from its `active_job` context variable) and `host` (from which
27	executor it is). Today only the package sync jobs pass `mutates`; `folder_sync` is #209.
28	"""
29	
30	from __future__ import annotations
31	
32	import logging
33	from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
34	
35	from rich.console import Console
36	from rich.panel import Panel
37	from rich.prompt import Prompt
38	from rich.text import Text
39	
40	from pcswitcher.confirmer import PausableUI
41	from pcswitcher.models import Host, SyncAbortedByUser
42	
43	__all__ = ["StepGate", "TerminalUIStepGate"]
44	
45	_PROCEED = "p"
46	_ABORT = "a"
47	
48	
49	@runtime_checkable
50	class StepGate(Protocol):
51	    """A per-action confirmation gate: show one pending modification, block, decide."""
52	
53	    async def confirm_action(self, *, job: str, host: Host, description: str, command: str) -> None:
54	        """Show a pending modification and block until the user decides.
55	
56	        Args:
57	            job: Name of the job about to modify something (panel heading, log context).
58	            host: Which machine the modification lands on.
59	            description: Short human phrase for what this achieves ("install firefox").
60	            command: The operation VERBATIM — the shell command as it will be executed, or
61	                a `send_file <local> -> <remote>` rendering for a transfer.
62	
63	        Returns:
64	            None when the user chose to proceed.
65	
66	        Raises:
67	            SyncAbortedByUser: The user aborted, or the prompt could not be answered
68	                (EOF / Ctrl-C). Never swallowed into a silent "proceed".
69	        """
70	        ...
71	
72	
73	class TerminalUIStepGate:
74	    """`StepGate` backed by the Rich console and the live `TerminalUI`.
75	
76	    Pauses the live display around the blocking prompt for the same reason
77	    `TerminalUIConfirmer` does — a Rich `Live` and a `Prompt.ask` cannot share the
78	    terminal — and resumes it in a `finally` so the display is handed back even when the
79	    prompt raises.
80	    """
81	
82	    def __init__(
83	        self,
84	        console: Console,
85	        ui: PausableUI,
86	        *,
87	        logger: logging.Logger | None = None,
88	    ) -> None:
89	        self._console = console
90	        self._ui = ui
91	        self._logger = logger if logger is not None else logging.getLogger("pcswitcher.step_gate")
92	
93	    async def confirm_action(self, *, job: str, host: Host, description: str, command: str) -> None:
94	        extra = {"job": job, "host": host.value}
95	
96	        # Body is assembled as a `Text`, never a markup string: `command` is arbitrary
97	        # content (package names, file paths, snippet bodies) and a stray `[` in it would
98	        # otherwise be parsed as Rich markup and raise mid-prompt.
99	        body = Text()
100	        body.append(f"{job} → {host.value}\n", style="bold")
101	        body.append(f"{description}\n\n", style="dim")
102	        body.append(command, style="bold")
103	
104	        self._ui.pause()
105	        try:
106	            self._console.print()
107	            self._console.print(Panel(body, title="Confirm modification", border_style="yellow"))
108	            self._console.print()
109	            # No `default=`: the user must type a choice. An accidental Enter re-prompts
110	            # rather than picking either outcome for them.
111	            response = Prompt.ask(
112	                f"[bold]Run this?[/bold] [{_PROCEED}] proceed  [{_ABORT}] abort sync",
113	                choices=[_PROCEED, _ABORT],
114	                show_choices=False,
115	            )
116	        except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt) as exc:
117	            # Unanswerable is not approval: the same rule the review applies to Ctrl-C.
118	            self._logger.warning("Confirmation prompt interrupted; aborting sync", extra=extra)
119	            raise SyncAbortedByUser(f"{job}: confirmation prompt interrupted before {description}") from exc
120	        finally:
121	            self._ui.resume()
122	
123	        if response == _ABORT:
124	            self._logger.warning("Aborted by user at: %s", description, extra=extra)
125	            raise SyncAbortedByUser(f"{job}: aborted by user before {description} on {host.value}")
126	        self._logger.debug("Confirmed: %s", description, extra=extra)

uv run python - <<'EOF'
import ast, pathlib
files = [
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_snap_sync.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_flatpak_sync.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_manual_installs_sync.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_items.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_review.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_state.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_sync_core.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_package_sync_candidate_selection.py",
 "tests/unit/test_step_gate.py",
 "tests/unit/orchestrator/test_snap_autorefresh_hold.py",
 "tests/unit/jobs/test_folder_sync.py",
 "tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py",
]
for f in files:
    p = pathlib.Path(f)
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"MISSING {f}"); continue
    tree = ast.parse(p.read_text())
    print(f"\n===== {f} =====")
    def walk(node, cls=None):
        for n in node.body:
            if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef):
                d = ast.get_docstring(n) or ""
                print(f"  ## {n.name}: {d.strip().splitlines()[0] if d else ''}")
                walk(n, n.name)
            elif isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and n.name.startswith("test"):
                d = ast.get_docstring(n) or ""
                first = " ".join(d.strip().split())[:220] if d else ""
                print(f"    - {n.name} (L{n.lineno}): {first}")
    walk(tree)
EOF

"""Throwaway probes: do skip-always decisions on block-state items survive to the next run?"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from pcswitcher.jobs.apt_sync import AptSyncJob
from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.items import DiffAction, ItemClass
from pcswitcher.jobs.snap_sync import SnapSyncJob
from pcswitcher.models import CommandResult
from tests.unit.jobs.test_apt_sync import make_context

DECISIONS_YAML = """
machine_specific:
  {item_id}:
    item_class: {item_class}
    label: some label
    reason: null
    recorded_at: '2026-07-25T00:00:00+00:00'
"""


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_probe_apt_hold_skip_always_next_run() -> None:
    """A decision file already holding `apt:hold:pkg-x` — is the hold diff suppressed?"""
    decisions = DECISIONS_YAML.format(item_id="apt:hold:pkg-x", item_class="apt_hold")
    context, _s, _t = make_context(
        source_responses={
            "apt-mark showmanual": CommandResult(0, "pkg-x\n", ""),
            "apt-mark showhold": CommandResult(0, "pkg-x\n", ""),
            "dpkg-query": CommandResult(0, "pkg-x\t1.0\n", ""),
            "cat ~/": CommandResult(0, decisions, ""),
        },
        target_responses={
            "apt-mark showmanual": CommandResult(0, "pkg-x\n", ""),
            "apt-mark showhold": CommandResult(0, "", ""),
            "dpkg-query": CommandResult(0, "pkg-x\t1.0\n", ""),
            "cat ~/": CommandResult(1, "", ""),
        },
    )
    plan = await AptSyncJob(context).plan()
    hold_diffs = [d for d in plan.diffs if d.item_class == ItemClass.APT_HOLD]
    print("APT hold diffs after skip-always:", hold_diffs)
    assert hold_diffs == [], f"LEAK: hold diff re-emitted despite recorded skip-always: {hold_diffs}"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_probe_snap_hold_skip_always_next_run() -> None:
    """A decision file already holding `snap:hold:foo` — is the snap hold diff suppressed?"""
    decisions = DECISIONS_YAML.format(item_id="snap:hold:foo", item_class="snap_hold")
    listing_held = "Name  Version  Rev  Tracking  Publisher  Notes\nfoo  1.0  10  latest/stable  x  held\n"
    listing_plain = "Name  Version  Rev  Tracking  Publisher  Notes\nfoo  1.0  10  latest/stable  x  -\n"
    context, _s, _t = make_context(
        source_responses={
            "snap list --all": CommandResult(0, listing_held, ""),
            "cat ~/": CommandResult(0, decisions, ""),
        },
        target_responses={
            "snap list --all": CommandResult(0, listing_plain, ""),
            "cat ~/": CommandResult(1, "", ""),
        },
    )
    plan = await SnapSyncJob(context).plan()
    hold_diffs = [d for d in plan.diffs if d.item_class == ItemClass.SNAP_HOLD]
    print("SNAP hold diffs after skip-always:", hold_diffs)
    assert hold_diffs == [], f"LEAK: snap hold diff re-emitted despite recorded skip-always: {hold_diffs}"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_probe_report_only_skip_always_records_nothing() -> None:
    """SKIP_ALWAYS on a REPORT_ONLY version-mismatch: is any decision file written?"""
    from pcswitcher.jobs.packages.review import Decision, ReviewOutcome

    context, source, _t = make_context(
        source_responses={
            "apt-mark showmanual": CommandResult(0, "pkg-v\n", ""),
            "dpkg-query": CommandResult(0, "pkg-v\t2.0\n", ""),
        },
        target_responses={
            "apt-mark showmanual": CommandResult(0, "pkg-v\n", ""),
            "dpkg-query": CommandResult(0, "pkg-v\t1.0\n", ""),
        },
    )
    job = AptSyncJob(context)
    plan = await job.plan()
    mismatch = [d for d in plan.diffs if d.action == DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY]
    print("report-only diffs:", mismatch)
    assert mismatch, "expected a version-mismatch REPORT_ONLY diff"
    job.accept_review(plan, ReviewOutcome(decisions={d.item_id: Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS for d in plan.diffs}, was_interactive=True))
    await job.apply()
    writes = [c.args[0] for c in source.run_command.call_args_list if "decisions.yaml" in c.args[0] and "mv -f" in c.args[0]]
    print("decision-file writes:", writes)
    assert writes, "GAP: SKIP_ALWAYS on a REPORT_ONLY item records nothing — it will re-appear every run"

# Phase 02 — package sync scenario/coverage matrix

Requirement-derived scenario enumeration for the four package jobs, mapped to pytest coverage. Branches come from ADR-020, 02-CONTEXT.md (D-01…D-33), 02-208-HOLD-MASK-REPLICATION.md and docs/jobs/package-sync.md — not from code paths, though code was read to decide what actually happens.

## Legend

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| U | covered by a unit test that asserts this branch |
| V | covered by the VM integration suite |
| P | partial — a neighbouring test exists, this branch is not asserted |
| — | no coverage |
| ‼ | verified defect or verified requirement gap (probed this session) |

Test file shorthand: `apt` = tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py · `snap` = test_snap_sync.py · `flat` = test_flatpak_sync.py · `man` = test_manual_installs_sync.py · `core` = test_package_sync_core.py · `rev` = test_package_review.py · `state` = test_package_state.py · `items` = test_package_items.py · `fold` = test_folder_sync.py · `hold` = tests/unit/orchestrator/test_snap_autorefresh_hold.py · `gate` = tests/unit/test_step_gate.py · `cfg` = tests/unit/orchestrator/test_config_system.py · `exit` = test_session_status_from_job_results.py · `INT` = tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py

## A. apt packages — presence and version diff (D-03, D-04, D-25)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | On source's manual set, absent on target, candidate exists | MISSING_ON_TARGET → INSTALL, default-ticked | U V | core:`test_missing_on_target_yields_install`, apt:`test_diff_yields_exactly_two_missing_items`, INT:`test_apt_sync_installs_missing_package` |
| A2 | On source, absent on target, target repos offer no candidate | REPO_UNAVAILABLE → REPORT_ONLY, never an install | U | core:`test_missing_and_unavailable_yields_repo_unavailable_not_install`, apt:`test_no_candidate_package_is_reported_not_installed` |
| A3 | On target's manual set only | EXTRA_ON_TARGET → REMOVE, own unticked group | U | core:`test_extra_on_target_yields_remove`, apt:`test_extra_on_target_yields_extra_on_target_remove` |
| A4 | Present both, equal version | no diff at all | U | core:`test_equal_versions_yields_no_diff` |
| A5 | Present both, versions differ | VERSION_MISMATCH → REPORT_ONLY naming both versions; never force-converged | U | core:`test_version_mismatch_yields_report_only_with_both_versions` |
| A6 | Version ordering (epoch, tilde, revision) | decided by `dpkg --compare-versions`, never string compare | U | items:`TestCompareDebVersions` (incl. real-dpkg cross-check) |
| A7 | Package pinned on target via preferences.d | HELD_OR_PINNED REPORT_ONLY echo on the package | U | core:`test_pin_fact_yields_held_or_pinned_distinguishable_from_a_hold_item`, apt:`test_preferences_d_pin_surfaces_with_pin_mechanism_and_filename` |
| A8 | Package held on target | install/upgrade action suppressed, no package-level report | U | core:`test_target_hold_only_yields_apt_hold_remove_and_suppresses_package_action`, apt:`test_held_package_yields_hold_item_not_duplicate_held_or_pinned_report` |
| A9 | Package pinned *and* a hold exists for another package | pin echo and hold item coexist, stay distinguishable | U | apt:`test_pin_still_yields_report_only_echo_alongside_a_hold_item` |
| A10 | Dependency-only package (not in `apt-mark showmanual`) | never in the manifest → never installed, never removed, never reported | P | implicit in capture (`showmanual` only); no test asserts an auto-installed package is invisible. **This is the mechanism the user's example 1 depends on.** |
| A11 | Same package is no-candidate on source *and* missing on target | surfaces twice: `manual_installs_sync` unreproducible item + `apt_sync` REPO_UNAVAILABLE report | — | no test; two managers describe one package in two reviews |
| A12 | `apt-mark showmanual` empty on a machine | empty manifest, no crash, no mass removal | P | `_resolve_versions` early-returns; no test for the empty-source→remove-everything shape |
| A13 | Version resolution source | `dpkg-query`, never `apt list --installed` | U | apt:`test_dpkg_query_used_not_apt_list_installed` |

## B. apt holds (#208 D1–D6)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Held on source, not target | `apt:hold:<pkg>` INSTALL → `sudo apt-mark hold` | U | apt:`test_source_held_yields_install_hold_item_and_converge_runs_apt_mark_hold`, core:`test_source_hold_only_yields_apt_hold_install` |
| B2 | Held on target, not source | REMOVE → `sudo apt-mark unhold`, unticked removal group | U | apt:`test_target_held_only_yields_remove_unhold_item` |
| B3 | Held on both / neither | no hold diff | U | apt:`test_held_on_both_yields_no_hold_diff`, core:`test_held_on_both_yields_no_diff` |
| B4 | Hold identity is distinct from package identity | two separate review items for one package | U | apt:`test_held_package_yields_hold_item_not_duplicate_held_or_pinned_report` |
| B5 | Review verb | group/entry read "hold"/"unhold", never "install"/"remove" | — | **no test asserts the group title or `action_label` for APT_HOLD/SNAP_HOLD/FLATPAK_MASK** — the crux of #208 D3 |
| B6 | Hold converges after the package install in the same run (D8) | install lands before its hold | — | snap has the equivalent test; apt does not |
| B7 | Hold approved for a package whose install was skipped (D6) | `apt-mark hold` on an absent package → normal per-item failure | — | no test; actual `apt-mark` exit behaviour for an unknown package unverified |
| B8 | skip-always on a hold item | DecisionEntry written on the holder's machine | U | apt:`test_skip_always_on_a_hold_writes_the_decision_file` |
| B9 | skip-always on a hold item, next run | item inert, no diff | ‼ | **BROKEN — verified.** `collect_hold_sets()` output never passes `filter_inert`, so the hold diff is re-emitted every run despite the recorded decision |
| B10 | Holds drive no `apt-get -s` simulation | selection state only | P | code filters to APT_PACKAGE; no test |
| B11 | `/usr/bin/apt-mark` in the target sudo grant | named in the hint | U | apt:`test_apt_mark_is_in_the_target_sudo_command_list` |

## C. apt repository config — sources, keys, pins, apt.conf (D-11, D-12, D-13, D-27)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Source file missing on target, key present on source | INSTALL | U | apt:`test_source_with_key_present_on_source_yields_plain_install` |

Per-manager diff taxonomies, the apt repo-group transaction (backup → write → update → rollback), D-30 collateral in all six variants, the snippet lifecycle including the non-additive push guard, review grouping/defaults/abort, dry-run, per-item failure isolation, exit-code derivation, folder_sync exclusions, the snapd hold window, and the new step gate are all covered — mostly at unit level, with 7 VM tests for whole-run contracts.

The hold/unhold item reappears in every later review. Flatpak masks *are* correct, so the three managers #208 D3 calls uniform are not.
2. **skip-always on any REPORT_ONLY item records nothing.** Version mismatches, repo-unavailable packages and pin echoes get the three-way choice and "skip always" silently no-ops (`_record_permanent_skips` filters to INSTALL/CHANGE/REMOVE). This one is code-verified but the snapd behaviour itself I did not exercise here.

- No "P was the only package from that source — remove the source and key too?" prompt. Source/key removals propagate only because those files vanished on the source machine, as independent unticked items.

- No test asserts a hold/mask renders as "Hold …"/"Unmask …" instead of under an install/remove group — the one behavioural promise of #208 D3.
- No idempotency test anywhere: converge once, second run shows an empty review.

options.description: Implement the third choice in the checkbox flow for INSTALL/CHANGE/REMOVE items, including holds and masks (docs promise it for those specifically). Leave REPORT_ONLY items informational and add an amending note to ADR-020 D-07 + docs saying so. Avoids the VERSION_MISMATCH problem: a version drift has no honest "holder", and recording it on the source would silently stop that package syncing entirely — far stronger than "stop reporting this".

options.label: Add it for every item incl. REPORT_ONLY
options.description: Full D-07 as literally written. Needs a new holder rule per diff class (repo-unavailable→source, held/pinned→target) and a decision on VERSION_MISMATCH, which has no correct holder — likely needs a separate "mute this report" concept rather than a machine-specific decision entry. Largest scope.

options.label: Docs only, defer the UI
options.description: Amend ADR-020 D-07 and docs/jobs/package-sync.md to describe the two choices that exist, and file an issue for the third. Already tracked in .planning/codebase/CONCERNS.md. Cheapest, but UAT then runs against docs that under-promise a designed feature.

questions.question: Classic-confinement snaps are confirmed uninstallable (zellij on this machine is classic; the check is per-revision so --revision doesn't bypass it). Scope of the fix?

options.label: Classic + devmode now (Recommended)
options.description: Parse the confinement token from the Notes column _parse_snap_list already splits, thread --classic/--devmode into install (and refresh). ~10-15 lines plus tests. Sideloaded snaps (x1 revisions) become a separate issue — they need a product decision on which diff class an unfetchable revision gets, and there are zero instances on this machine to test against.

options.label: Classic + devmode + sideload
options.description: Also classify x<N>-revision snaps as REPORT_ONLY/unreproducible instead of emitting an unsatisfiable install. ~30-45 lines. Needs a decision on the diff class now, and cannot be verified locally — no sideloaded snaps exist on this machine.

options.label: File an issue, fix later
options.description: Keep the branch focused on Phase 2 as planned. Cost: snap_sync reports FAILED on every run for any user with a classic snap — which is most developer CLIs (code, go, node, kubectl, helm) — until fixed.

Verdicts are in. One correction to what I told you earlier.

## Challenge results

**Hold skip-always leak — CONFIRMED, and worse than I reported.** apt and snap both, in both directions; flatpak masks are correct (the control held). `_record_permanent_skips` writes the right id to the right machine, and nothing ever reads it back. The part I missed: the *add* direction returns **default-checked**, because `install` isn't a removal action — so a user who bulk-accepts the install group re-applies the very hold they permanently declined. Fix is in flight.

**REPORT_ONLY skip-always — my finding was wrong as stated.** No user can reach that branch: the checkbox review can only ever produce apply or skip-once. But the challenge turned up something bigger — **the checkbox UI never renders a "skip always" choice for *any* regular item**, while ADR-020 D-07 and `docs/jobs/package-sync.md` (lines 40-44, and 107 specifically for holds/masks) promise a three-way choice. So the promise is undelivered across every item class, not just informational ones. It's already logged in `.planning/codebase/CONCERNS.md:206` with stale file paths. That's now being implemented for actionable items per your decision.

**Classic snaps — CONFIRMED.** `zellij` on this machine is classic; snapd's refusal is per-*revision*, so `--revision=N` doesn't bypass it. The failure is graceful (clean per-item failure, run continues), but it means a permanently red `snap_sync` on every run. Useful detail found: passing `--classic` to a strict snap is only a warning, not an error.

## In flight

Seven agents: snap/flatpak gap tests **done** (commit `f2c8743e`, 15 tests, no xfails); apt tests, core/state/manual tests, CLI-gate + `mutates=` audit, the hold-skip-always fix, the skip-always review UI, and VM integration tests still running. The classic/devmode snap fix is queued behind the hold fix — both edit `snap_sync.py`, so I'm serializing them rather than letting two agents clobber the file.

## New finding from the completed agent

**Flatpak remote removal has no dependency guard.** `_remote_ready_on_target` gates only the *install* direction. A target-only remote is offered for deletion with no awareness that a target-side ref names it as origin — and because that ref exists identically on both machines it produces no diff at all, so it's never even shown. Converging the removal orphans it. Behaviour is now pinned by a test; it wants a GitHub issue, not a silent fix — say the word and I'll file it.

Also flagged: two pre-existing `F401` lint errors in `test_apt_sync.py` from the in-flight apt agent — its own lint gate will catch them before it commits.

Repo: /home/janfr/dev/pc-switcher, branch gsd/phase-02-package-management-sync. Fix a CONFIRMED defect.

## Ownership

You own `src/pcswitcher/jobs/snap_sync.py`, `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/items.py` and `tests/unit/jobs/test_snap_sync.py`. Other agents are concurrently editing `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/review.py`, `tests/unit/jobs/test_manual_installs_sync.py`, `test_package_state.py`, `test_package_sync_core.py`, `test_package_review.py`, `tests/unit/test_step_gate.py`, `tests/unit/cli/*` and `tests/integration/*` — do not touch any of those. Run repo-wide `ruff format`/`ruff check --fix` ONLY scoped to your own files (`uv run ruff format src/pcswitcher/jobs/snap_sync.py ...`), never repo-wide: it would reformat other agents' uncommitted work.

## The confirmed defect

`snap_sync` cannot install classic-confinement snaps. `_converge_install` (`src/pcswitcher/jobs/snap_sync.py:423-441`) emits `sudo snap install --revision={rev} {name}` with no `--classic`. Verified against this machine:

- `man snap` and `snap install --help`: "Installation of snaps built with classic confinement requires explicit confirmation by passing `--classic`."
- snapd binary strings: `This revision of snap %q was published using classic confinement and thus may…` / `If you understand and want to proceed repeat the command including --classic.` and `snap %q requires classic confinement`. Note **"This revision"** — the check is per-revision, so `--revision=N` does NOT bypass it.
- Same shape for devmode: `If you understand and want to proceed repeat the command including --devmode;`.
- Blast radius here: of 17 installed snaps, `zellij` is classic (its `snap list` Notes column reads `classic`; `snap list --all` shows `zellij 43 disabled,classic`). Classic is the norm for developer CLIs (code, go, node, kubectl, helm).

Issue **#214** filed for the flatpak remote orphaning. The fix goes out as soon as the running test agent releases `test_flatpak_sync.py` — I'm serializing rather than risking a clobber.

## Sideloaded snaps — what they are and why they break

Normally a snap comes from the Snap Store, and every published revision has a store-assigned number (`zellij` is revision 65 on this machine). But you can also install a snap straight from a local `.snap` file — `snap install --dangerous ./foo.snap`, or `snap try` during development. There's no store revision for that, so snapd assigns a **local** one, rendered with an `x` prefix: `x1`, `x2`, and so on. The `x` literally means "these bytes came from a file, not the store."

pc-switcher captures name + channel + revision from `snap list` on the source, then converges the target with `snap install --revision=<N>`. For a sideloaded snap that becomes:

```
sudo snap install --revision=x1 foo
```

on the target — and the store has no revision `x1` of `foo`, because that revision only ever existed as a file on the source machine's disk. It fails. Every run, forever, with review text that gives the user no hint what to do. Sideloaded snaps also usually track no channel, so the channel switch that follows would be equally meaningless.

It's structurally the same defect as the classic-confinement bug just fixed: captured state turned into a command that cannot succeed. The difference is the classic case had an obvious right answer (pass `--classic`), and this one doesn't — which is why I flagged it as needing your decision rather than folding it in. The plausible options are treating an `x<N>` revision as **unreproducible** and routing it to `manual_installs_sync` (which already owns "things no package manager can reproduce", and where an install snippet could carry the actual `.snap` file), or emitting a **REPORT_ONLY** diff that names the fact without proposing a doomed command.

Detection is trivial (`revision.startswith("x")`). What's missing is the product call, and the fact that there are zero sideloaded snaps on this machine to test against.

How common: uncommon for most users, but it shows up with locally-built snaps, vendor betas shipped as files, and anything installed with `snap try`. Worth knowing whether you have any before deciding how much it matters — `snap list | awk '$3 ~ /^x/'` on both machines will tell you.

Once the flatpak fix lands I'll run the full gate and push to PR 206.

## The defect

`flatpak_sync` offers a target-only remote for removal with no awareness that installed refs on the target still name it as their origin; approving the removal orphans them. The install direction IS guarded (`_converge_ref` → `_remote_ready_on_target`, `src/pcswitcher/jobs/flatpak_sync.py:667` and `:716`); the remove direction has none — `_diff_flatpak_remotes` (`:328`) emits the REMOVE diff from presence alone and `_converge_remote`'s REMOVE branch (`:639`) runs `flatpak remote-delete` unconditionally.

What makes it dangerous: the dependent ref is often installed identically on BOTH machines, so it produces no diff and never appears in the review. The user approves a remote deletion whose `detail` is `None` — nothing states the consequence.

## Required approach

Follow the apt collateral pattern (D-30, `docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-package-convergence.md`), NOT the install direction's hard refusal:

- At **plan time**, for each remote REMOVE diff, determine which of the TARGET's installed refs name that remote as their origin, in that same scope. `plan()` already queries the target's refs (`query_target_items()`); reuse what is in hand rather than issuing new commands — do not add a per-remote query.

- Do NOT refuse the removal outright. Blanket refusal would block a legitimate cleanup where the refs are being removed in the same run. D-30's reasoning applies verbatim: the decision belongs in the review, informed, never as a mid-apply refusal.
- Scope matters: a remote is per-installation, so only refs in the SAME scope count as dependents. Do not cross user/system.
- A remote with no dependent refs keeps `detail=None` — no noise.

Consider whether refs approved for removal in the same run should be excluded from the dependent list. If you can do that cleanly from state already available at plan time, do it and note it; if it needs new plumbing, leave it and say so in your report rather than half-building it.

def _maybe_check_for_update(console: Console, *, no_version_check: bool) -> None:
    """Best-effort startup check for a newer stable release; offer to upgrade inline.

    Non-fatal ONLY up to the point the on-disk installation is modified. Once
    `uv tool install` runs, the current process may be stale (a later lazy
    import would load a mismatched new module), so we must not keep executing:
    on a successful upgrade we re-exec the new binary, and on any failure after
    the install started we exit and tell the user how to recover. Everything
    before that boundary (check failure, offline, declined prompt, or `uv` not
    even launchable) warns and lets the current command proceed.

    Skips entirely for `--no-version-check`, `PCSWITCHER_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK`, a
    help request (`--help`/`-h`), and non-interactive runs (either stdin or
    stdout not a TTY).

    Args:
        console: Rich console to print status to.
        no_version_check: If True, skip the check (from `--no-version-check`).

    Raises:
        typer.Exit: After the install has touched disk and either failed
            (recover via `self update`) or succeeded but the automatic restart
            could not happen (re-run the command). Never raised before the

Confirmed — your hypothesis is right, and my earlier explanation was wrong.

**Local:** `0.5.1.post16.dev0+05d8293` — resolves against the `v0.5.1` tag, so it's *newer* than 0.5.1 and no upgrade is offered.

**CI:** `0.0.0+post.1.dev.0.63837dc` — that `0.0.0` is dunamai's "no tags found" fallback. `actions/checkout@v7` defaults to `fetch-depth: 1` and fetches no tags, so uv-dynamic-versioning has nothing to resolve against. Then `0.0.0 < 0.5.1` → "a new stable version is available" → prompt → abort.

So it doesn't fail *sometimes* — in CI it fails **always**, and would have from the moment that test was written. My "only when a newer release exists" was the right mechanism described against the wrong version number.

That raises a question my fix doesn't answer: what else in CI sees version `0.0.0`?

content.text:
Answered — and the blast radius is smaller than I feared:

**`integration-tests.yml` already uses `fetch-depth: 0`** (line 66), so tags are present and the version resolves properly there. That matters, because `install_on_target.validate` compares `target_version > source_version` and errors on a conflict — with a `0.0.0` source that comparison would misbehave on every VM run. It doesn't, because that workflow was set up correctly.

**`ci.yml` (lint + unit) uses the default shallow checkout**, so every job there sees `0.0.0+post.N.dev.0.<sha>`. The only test that read the version was the one that just broke; everything else is version-agnostic, which is why CI showed exactly one failure.

So my fix is at the right level — the test shouldn't depend on version resolution at all — but there's a latent trap: any future unit test or code path that compares versions will silently see `0.0.0` in CI and be wrong in a way that's invisible locally. Adding `fetch-depth: 0` to `ci.yml` would close that for roughly zero cost on a repo this size. It's a CI-config change outside this phase's scope, so I haven't touched it — say the word if you want it.

One unrelated thing I noticed: your local venv reports `0.5.1.post16.dev0` while HEAD is 153 commits past `v0.5.1` — the stale version stamp. `uv sync --reinstall-package pcswitcher` re-stamps it if the number ever matters to you.

Both integration failures are in **my new tests**, and both are test bugs, not product bugs. More importantly:

**#208 D9 is answered — the assumption holds.** `TestSnapHoldCaptureTiming` passed against real snapd: a system-wide `refresh.hold` does not mask per-snap `held` notes. And `TestBlockStateDecisionRoundTrip` passed, so the hold skip-always fix works end-to-end on real machines.

Now your point about the patch. You're right, and the reason other tests don't break is damning for what I did:

`tests/unit/cli/test_version_check.py` fakes a TTY in ~10 tests — and every one of them also patches `get_this_version` **and** `get_highest_release`. They never let real version resolution or a real network call happen. Mine was the only test that faked a TTY and then let the actual update check run. So the repo already had a convention and I bypassed it with an env var.

Reverting the patch and fixing the root cause:

lint:
    name: Lint
    needs: check-changes
    if: needs.check-changes.outputs.should-run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Full history: uv-dynamic-versioning derives the version from the nearest tag, and
      # a shallow checkout fetches none — the package then builds as 0.0.0+post.N.dev.0.<sha>,
      # which reads as older than every release.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

"""The running package's version must be derived from a git tag, never the 0.0.0 fallback.

Deliberately not a unit test: it asserts a property of the ENVIRONMENT the package was
built in, which a unit test would have to mock away to stay hermetic. It needs no VMs
either — it lives here because `tests/integration/` is the phase whose checkout fetches
full history (`fetch-depth: 0`), which is exactly the condition under test.

`uv-dynamic-versioning` derives the version from the nearest reachable tag. A checkout
that fetches no tags leaves it nothing to resolve against, and it falls back to
`0.0.0+post.<n>.dev.0.<sha>` — a version that silently reads as OLDER than every release.
Two real behaviours break on that, neither of them noisily:

- `InstallOnTargetJob.validate` refuses to run when the target's version is newer than the
  source's; a `0.0.0` source inverts that comparison against any real target.
- The startup update check offers an upgrade to the newest release and, on a TTY, blocks
  on its prompt — which is how this was found.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess

from pcswitcher.version import Version, get_this_version

# The version dunamai produces when no tag is reachable. Compared on the release triple
# alone: the fallback's local/dev suffix carries the commit sha, which varies per run.
_NO_TAG_FALLBACK = Version.parse("0.0.0")


def test_version_resolves_from_a_tag_not_the_no_tag_fallback() -> None:
    """A tagless checkout yields 0.0.0 and silently reads as older than every release."""
    version = get_this_version()

    assert (version.major, version.minor, version.patch) != (
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.major,
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.minor,
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.patch,
    ), (
        f"pc-switcher resolved to {version.semver_str()}, uv-dynamic-versioning's "
        "no-tag fallback. The checkout fetched no tags — a workflow step is missing "
        "`fetch-depth: 0`. Every version comparison in this run is against a version "
        "that reads as older than every release."
    )

## How I read the key, and how I verified it

All experiments ran in throwaway `ubuntu:24.04` docker containers (flatpak 1.14.6, libostree 2024.5) — nothing touched this machine's flatpak state. Read-only `flatpak remote-add --help` locally.

**Trust is read two ways, both flatpak/ostree-native and both working per scope:**
- **gpg-verify** → `flatpak remotes {--user|--system} --columns=name,url,options`. The `options` column prints a comma-separated token list containing `no-gpg-verify` exactly when verification is off; a remote with no options prints only two fields with **no** trailing tab (parser accepts 2 or 3 fields).
- **the key** → `sha256sum <installation>/repo/<remote>.trustedkeys.gpg`, one batched glob per scope (`$HOME/.local/share/flatpak/repo`, `/var/lib/flatpak/repo`). Rejected `ostree remote gpg-list-keys`: the subcommand only prints key *info*, not exportable bytes, and the `ostree` binary is not installed alongside flatpak on Ubuntu (confirmed absent on this dev box). The system keyring is 0644 in a 0755 dir, so an unprivileged `sha256sum` reads it (verified as a non-root user in-container).

**Verified live:** `--gpg-import=<source's trustedkeys.gpg>` is accepted and makes installs work; the resulting target keyring is **byte-identical** to the source's, and re-importing is idempotent — so the digest comparison converges instead of looping. Importing over a *different* existing key produces a union (digests then stay unequal; documented as reported-as-found). `remote-modify` accepts `--url` + `--gpg-import` + `--gpg-verify` in one command (`remote-add` has no `--gpg-verify`, hence the two flag shapes). `remote-delete` removes the keyring. Remote names may contain dots, so only the fixed suffix is stripped.

## Diff class for a key change

`DiffAction.CHANGE` / `DiffClass.VERSION_MISMATCH` — the same class a differing URL already used, and the comparison is now whole-item equality (url, gpg_verify, key_digest), so name+scope stay identity. One `remote-modify` carries url and trust together; no REMOVE+INSTALL churn. The item carries a **digest**, not key bytes (bytes travel by `send_file`, staged at `~/.cache/pc-switcher/flatpak-staging/`, discarded in a `finally`) — matching `AptKeyItem`'s digest+transfer split, justified in the dataclass docstring.

## The trust anchor is gone

Removing it required one more change than the issue anticipated: each VM generated its **own** signing key, so pc1's key could never verify pc2's local repo — the anchor was hiding that too. `vm-test-fixtures.sh` now imports one embedded, passphrase-less key on both VMs (fingerprint `24DE0AA0…`), installs nothing under `/usr/share/ostree/trusted.gpg.d`, and deletes the legacy anchor on version upgrade. `FIXTURES_VERSION`/`PCSWITCHER_TEST_FIXTURES_VERSION` bumped to 2 (forces a baseline rebuild). I ran the reworked script end-to-end in a container (builds, installs, second run is a no-op) and separately simulated the two-machine flow: with no anchor, name+url-only **fails** (`Can't check signature: public key not found`) and name+url+key **succeeds**. Flathub provisioning was not needed.

## Unverified without a VM

- The integration test itself (`test_flatpak_installs_into_source_scope_after_remote`) has not run — VM suite unavailable, and integration CI only triggers on PRs targeting `main`.
- The fixture script was exercised in a container as root with a `sudo` shim path, with the snap section skipped; the snap half and the real `sudo`/baseline-snapshot interaction are unverified.
- The `$HOME` expansion for the user-scope repo path over a real non-login SSH exec channel is assumed from `apt_sync._target_home_dir`'s established use, not re-measured.
- Real-world remotes (Flathub) were not exercised — only local `file://` repos.

Verification: `ruff format`/`check`, `codespell`, `basedpyright` (0 errors), `pytest tests/unit` (1133 passed), `pytest tests/integration --collect-only -m ""` (80 collected).</result>

Pushed (`3bcb28f3`), PR body carries `Closes #215`. Two integration runs will go back to back — the v1 one already in flight, then this one with fixtures v2.

## The fix

`FlatpakRemoteItem` now carries `gpg_verify` and a **key digest**; the key bytes travel by `send_file`, staged under `~/.cache/pc-switcher/flatpak-staging/` and cleaned up in a `finally` — the same digest-plus-transfer split `AptKeyItem` already uses, which keeps ADR-020 D-12's "keys travel byte-for-byte, never re-fetched" rule intact for flatpak too.

Everything was verified live in throwaway `ubuntu:24.04` containers, not reasoned about:

- Trust reads two ways, both per scope: `flatpak remotes --columns=name,url,options` (the `options` column prints `no-gpg-verify` exactly when verification is off), and `sha256sum` over `<installation>/repo/<remote>.trustedkeys.gpg`.
- `ostree remote gpg-list-keys` was **rejected on evidence** — it prints key info, not exportable bytes, and `ostree` isn't even installed alongside flatpak on Ubuntu.
- Re-importing the same key is idempotent and produces a **byte-identical** keyring, so the digest comparison converges instead of oscillating. Importing a *different* key produces a union, so digests stay unequal — reported as found rather than silently normalised.
- A key change is `CHANGE`/`VERSION_MISMATCH`, same as a URL change, and one `remote-modify` carries url and trust together.

The two-machine flow was simulated directly: with no anchor, name+url-only **fails** with `Can't check signature: public key not found`; name+url+key **succeeds**. So the test now proves the key travels, and your 268 MB Flathub fallback wasn't needed.

## What's still unproven

The integration test itself has never executed — that's what these two CI runs are for. Also unverified without a VM: the fixture script's snap half and its real `sudo`/baseline-snapshot interaction (it was exercised in a container as root with a `sudo` shim, snap section skipped), and `$HOME` expansion for the user-scope repo path over a real non-login SSH channel, which is assumed from `apt_sync._target_home_dir`'s established use rather than re-measured.

Real Flathub was never exercised — only local `file://` repos. If Flathub's trust layout differs from a plain signed OSTree repo in some way this doesn't cover, that would show up only against the real thing.

`snap get system refresh.hold` requires admin auth. Run as an unprivileged user it does not return "empty" — it **fails with `access denied (try with sudo)`** and prints nothing to stdout. `_capture_snap_hold` therefore returns `None` on every run, on every machine, unconditionally.

Environment: pc2, Ubuntu 24.04, **snapd/snap 2.76.1**.

### Evidence

Baseline (no hold set), as `testuser`:

```
$ snap get system refresh.hold          rc=1  stdout=[]  stderr=[error: access denied (try with sudo)]
$ sudo snap get system refresh.hold     rc=0  stdout=[]
  state.json core.config.refresh = {"hold": ""}
```

The exact orchestrator command, then read-back three ways:

```
$ sudo snap set system refresh.hold="$(date -u -d '+6 hours' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"   rc=0
$ snap get system refresh.hold          rc=1  stdout=[]  stderr=[error: access denied (try with sudo)]
$ sudo snap get system refresh.hold     rc=0  stdout=[2026-07-26T15:50:19Z]
  state.json core.config.refresh = {"hold": "2026-07-26T15:50:19Z"}
$ snap refresh --time                   (no sudo)
  timer: 00:00~24:00/4
  last: today at 11:47 CEST
  hold: today at 17:50 CEST
  next: today at 13:14 CEST (but held)
```

snapd authoritatively reports the hold in force (`hold:` line, `next: ... (but held)`), and it persists in `/var/lib/snapd/state.json`. **The pause works.** The per-snap `hello` hold from the CI run is irrelevant — my baseline had no per-snap hold and the read failed identically.

### Consequence in production (the real bug)

`orchestrator.py:1317` (`_capture_snap_hold`) always returns `None` → `_hold_snap_autorefresh` records "no prior hold" on both hosts → `_restore_snap_hold` takes the `prior is None` branch and runs `sudo snap set system refresh.hold=""` on **both** machines in `_cleanup`. Any hold the user set themselves (`snap refresh --hold`, an admin-set `refresh.hold`, incl. `forever`) is silently destroyed by every sync. Nothing warns: the `snap set` exits 0, and the failing `snap get` is swallowed by `result.success and value`.

Same defect, informational only, at `src/pcswitcher/jobs/snap_sync.py:667-670` — validate() logs `snap refresh.hold: (none)` for both hosts on every run regardless of actual state.

The CI failure is the same root cause in the test helper: `tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py:601-607` `_capture_system_refresh_hold` also omits sudo, so `assert engaged is not None` can never pass. Its `_restore_system_refresh_hold` mirrors the destructive `refresh.hold=""` write.

### Documented rule / mechanism (sources)

- Access control: snapd `daemon/api_snap_conf.go:39-45` — `/v2/snaps/{name}/conf` has `ReadAccess: authenticatedAccess{Polkit: polkitActionManageConfiguration}`. The shipped policy (`/usr/share/polkit-1/actions/io.snapcraft.snapd.policy` on pc2, identical to snapd `data/polkit/io.snapcraft.snapd.policy`) sets `io.snapcraft.snapd.manage-configuration` to `allow_any=auth_admin`, `allow_inactive=auth_admin`, `allow_active=auth_admin_keep`. **Reading** snap config is admin-gated in every case — so this is not an SSH artifact: on a real desktop seat it would raise an interactive polkit prompt a non-interactive sync cannot satisfy.
- `system` is an alias for `core`: verified — `sudo snap set core refresh.hold=<ts>` is read back identically by `sudo snap get system refresh.hold`. No historic distinction remains at 2.76.1.
- snapd only clears `refresh.hold` when it has **expired** (`overlord/snapstate/autorefresh.go`: `clearRefreshHold()` called from `Ensure()` in the "expired hold case" branch). It does not clear or reject an in-future hold.
- Format: `configcore/refresh.go:81-89` — value must be RFC3339 or the literal `forever`, else `snap set` errors out. The orchestrator's `+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` is accepted.
- No cap at set time: `+200 days` was stored and reported verbatim (`hold: 2027-02-11`). `maxPostponement = 95 * 24h` (`autorefresh.go:53`) constrains gating-snap holds (`autorefresh_gating.go:474-475` explicitly exempts `holdingSnap == "system"`), not the general config option. A 6-hour hold is nowhere near any limit.

### Read-back semantics with sudo (all confirmed)

| state | `sudo snap get system refresh.hold` |
|---|---|
| timestamp set | rc=0, `2026-07-26T15:50:19Z` |
| `forever` | rc=0, `forever` |
| set to `""` (what restore writes) | rc=0, empty stdout |
| key removed (`refresh.hold!`) | rc=1, `error: snap "core" has no "refresh.hold" configuration option` |

`snap refresh --time` works **unprivileged** and reveals the hold (`hold: today at 17:50 CEST` / `hold: forever` / `hold: 2027-02-11`), but the value is localized human text, not RFC3339 — usable as a human-readable log line, not as a capture/restore value.

### Correct sequence on this snapd (not implemented, as instructed)

- Capture: `sudo snap get system refresh.hold` — existing `value if result.success and value else None` logic is then correct for all four states above.
- Apply: unchanged, `sudo snap set system refresh.hold="$(date -u -d '+6 hours' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"` — already works.
- Restore: unchanged shape, but it only becomes safe once capture is privileged.
- Unprivileged verification (e.g. a validate-time log): `snap refresh --time`.

Worth noting separately: the same silent-swallow pattern means `_apply_snap_hold`'s WARNING would not have caught this class of failure either; a post-set verification would.
